import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Barnette's conjecture

Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic bipartite 3-connected planar graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle.

Mathlib has no notion of a planar graph. We define one here: a graph is planar if it has a
drawing in the Euclidean plane without crossings. Vertices are drawn as distinct points and
edges as Jordan arcs. An arc passes through no vertex other than its endpoints, and the arcs of
two distinct edges meet only at common endpoints.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Barnette's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnette%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia list entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ba69] Barnette, D. W., *Conjecture 5*, in Tutte, W. T. (ed.), *Recent Progress in
  Combinatorics: Proceedings of the Third Waterloo Conference on Combinatorics, May 1968*,
  Academic Press (1969).
-/

open SimpleGraph EuclideanGeometry

namespace BarnettesConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/--
A drawing of the simple graph `G` in the Euclidean plane without crossings.

Vertices are drawn as distinct points. The edge `uv` is drawn as a Jordan arc `arc h` from the
point of `u` to the point of `v`, where `h : G.Adj u v`; the arc of `vu` is the reverse of the
arc of `uv`. An arc passes through no vertex other than its two endpoints, and the arcs of two
distinct edges meet only at vertices, hence only at common endpoints.
-/
structure PlanarEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point at which the vertex `v` is drawn. -/
  toFun : V → ℝ²
  injective : Function.Injective toFun
  /-- The arc along which the edge `uv` is drawn. -/
  arc ⦃u v : V⦄ : G.Adj u v → _root_.Path (toFun u) (toFun v)
  arc_injective ⦃u v : V⦄ (h : G.Adj u v) : Function.Injective (arc h)
  arc_symm ⦃u v : V⦄ (h : G.Adj u v) : arc h.symm = (arc h).symm
  eq_of_mem_range_arc ⦃u v : V⦄ (h : G.Adj u v) ⦃w : V⦄ :
    toFun w ∈ Set.range (arc h) → w = u ∨ w = v
  range_arc_inter_subset ⦃u v x y : V⦄ (h : G.Adj u v) (h' : G.Adj x y) :
    s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) → Set.range (arc h) ∩ Set.range (arc h') ⊆ Set.range toFun

/-- A simple graph is planar if it has a drawing in the Euclidean plane without crossings. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (PlanarEmbedding G)

/-- A graph without edges is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_bot (n : ℕ) : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :=
  ⟨{
    toFun := fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.single 0 (i : ℝ)
    injective := fun i j hij ↦ by
      have : ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) = (j : ℕ) := by
        simpa [EuclideanSpace.single_apply] using congrArg (· 0) hij
      exact Fin.ext (by exact_mod_cast this)
    arc := fun _ _ h ↦ h.elim
    arc_injective := fun _ _ h ↦ h.elim
    arc_symm := fun _ _ h ↦ h.elim
    eq_of_mem_range_arc := fun _ _ h ↦ h.elim
    range_arc_inter_subset := fun _ _ _ _ h ↦ h.elim }⟩

/--
**Barnette's conjecture** (Barnette, 1969).

Every cubic bipartite 3-connected planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. That is, if a finite
simple graph $G$ is $3$-regular, bipartite, $3$-vertex-connected and planar, then $G$ has a cycle
that passes through each of its vertices exactly once.

Here $3$-vertex-connected means that $G$ has more than $3$ vertices and stays connected after
the removal of any set of fewer than $3$ vertices. By Steinitz's theorem, the $3$-connected
planar graphs are exactly the polyhedral graphs, so the hypotheses say that $G$ is a bipartite
cubic polyhedral graph.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem barnettes_conjecture [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbip : G.IsBipartite) (hconn : G.IsKConnected 3)
    (hplanar : IsPlanar G) : G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end BarnettesConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct; the notes' remarks (3-connectivity forcing ≥ 4 vertices, harmlessness of the IsHamiltonian convention, need for a bespoke planarity definition) all check out.
modeling_decisions: Planarity is defined topologically (the Wikipedia article's own definition: 'can be embedded into the Euclidean plane without any crossings'), not via Kuratowski/Wagner minors: `PlanarEmbedding G` consists of an injective vertex placement `toFun : V → ℝ²` (ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), via the repo's scoped `EuclideanGeometry` notation), for each adjacency `h : G.Adj u v` an injective `Path (toFun u) (toFun v)` (a Jordan arc), the condition that any vertex point lying on an arc is one of its two endpoints, and the condition that arcs of distinct edges (`s(u,v) ≠ s(x,y)`) intersect only in vertex points (hence, with the previous condition, only in common endpoints). `IsPlanar G := Nonempty (PlanarEmbedding G)`.

The field `arc_symm : arc h.symm = (arc h).symm` fixes the convention that the arc of vu is the reverse of the arc of uv. It is a normalisation only: the existence of a `PlanarEmbedding` is unchanged with or without it (choose one orientation per edge and reverse for the other), so it does not affect the class of planar graphs.

3-connectivity uses the repository's `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Connectivity.lean): `3 < Fintype.card V ∧ ∀ S : Finset V, S.card < 3 → (G.induce Sᶜ).Connected`. This is the standard definition of k-vertex-connectivity (Wikipedia's 'polyhedral = 3-vertex-connected planar'); it forces at least 4 vertices, ruling out the empty graph and other degenerate cases. It is satisfiable (e.g. the cube graph), so the theorem is not vacuous.

Graphs are finite simple graphs (`SimpleGraph V`, `[Fintype V]`), matching the setting of the conjecture (polyhedral graphs are finite and simple). `[DecidableEq V]` and `[DecidableRel G.Adj]` are only needed for Mathlib's `degree`/`IsHamiltonian` and carry no mathematical content.

The conclusion is Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` (`Fintype.card V ≠ 1 → ∃ a (p : G.Walk a a), p.IsHamiltonianCycle`). Its singleton convention is unreachable here because 3-connectivity forces more than 3 vertices, so the conclusion is exactly 'G has a Hamiltonian cycle'.
Cubic is formalised as `G.IsRegularOfDegree 3` (every vertex has degree exactly 3); bipartite as Mathlib's `G.IsBipartite` (abbreviation of `G.Colorable 2`).

A small `@[category test]` lemma `isPlanar_bot` (edgeless graphs on `Fin n` are planar) is included as basic API for the bespoke definition, per CONTRIBUTING.md. The Kelmans equivalent form, the dual tree-partition form and the Barnette–Goodey conjecture are not stated since the list entry does not pose them.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Barnette's conjecture

Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle. Equivalently, every bipartite polyhedral graph with three edges per vertex
is Hamiltonian.

A finite simple graph is *planar* if it can be drawn in the Euclidean plane without crossings.
Mathlib has no notion of planarity, so this file defines a plane drawing directly: vertices go
to distinct points of $\mathbb{R}^2$, every edge is drawn as an arc (an injective continuous
curve) joining the images of its ends, arcs pass through no vertex except at their ends, and two
distinct arcs meet only at vertices. A planar graph is *polyhedral* if it is 3-vertex-connected.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Barnette's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnette%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ba69] Barnette, David W., *Conjecture 5*, in Tutte, W. T. (ed.), Recent Progress in
  Combinatorics, Academic Press (1969).
-/

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval

namespace BarnettesConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A drawing of the simple graph `G` in the Euclidean plane without crossings. Vertices are
mapped injectively to points of $\mathbb{R}^2$, each edge is drawn as an arc (an injective
continuous curve) between the images of its two ends, no arc passes through the image of a vertex
other than at its ends, and two distinct arcs meet only at images of vertices (hence only at
common ends). -/
structure PlaneEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point of the plane representing each vertex. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The arc drawing each edge, parametrised by the unit interval. -/
  edge : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  edge_continuous (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (edge e)
  edge_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (edge e)
  /-- The ends of the arc of an edge are the images of the ends of that edge. -/
  edge_ends (e : G.edgeSet) : s(edge e 0, edge e 1) = Sym2.map vertex e
  /-- An arc passes through no vertex other than at its ends. -/
  edge_interior (e : G.edgeSet) (t : I) (ht₀ : t ≠ 0) (ht₁ : t ≠ 1) :
    edge e t ∉ Set.range vertex
  /-- Two distinct arcs meet only at vertices. -/
  edge_meet (e e' : G.edgeSet) (hee' : e ≠ e') (t t' : I) (h : edge e t = edge e' t') :
    edge e t ∈ Set.range vertex

/-- A simple graph is planar if it has a drawing in the Euclidean plane without crossings. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop := Nonempty (PlaneEmbedding G)

/-- A graph with no edges on at most one vertex is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_bot [Subsingleton V] : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) :=
  ⟨{ vertex := fun _ ↦ 0
     vertex_injective := fun _ _ _ ↦ Subsingleton.elim _ _
     edge := fun e ↦ absurd e.2 (by simp)
     edge_continuous := fun e ↦ absurd e.2 (by simp)
     edge_injective := fun e ↦ absurd e.2 (by simp)
     edge_ends := fun e ↦ absurd e.2 (by simp)
     edge_interior := fun e ↦ absurd e.2 (by simp)
     edge_meet := fun e ↦ absurd e.2 (by simp) }⟩

/-- A subgraph of a planar graph is planar. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPlanar.mono {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsPlanar H := by
  obtain ⟨D⟩ := hG
  let ι : H.edgeSet → G.edgeSet := Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG)
  have hι : Function.Injective ι := Set.inclusion_injective _
  exact ⟨{ vertex := D.vertex
           vertex_injective := D.vertex_injective
           edge := fun e ↦ D.edge (ι e)
           edge_continuous := fun e ↦ D.edge_continuous (ι e)
           edge_injective := fun e ↦ D.edge_injective (ι e)
           edge_ends := fun e ↦ D.edge_ends (ι e)
           edge_interior := fun e ↦ D.edge_interior (ι e)
           edge_meet := fun e e' hee' ↦ D.edge_meet (ι e) (ι e') (hι.ne hee') }⟩

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/--
**Barnette's conjecture.** Every cubic (3-regular) bipartite 3-vertex-connected planar finite
simple graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

Here `IsKConnected G 3` means that $G$ has more than three vertices and stays connected after
the removal of any two vertices; planar graphs with this property are the polyhedral graphs.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem barnettes_conjecture (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbip : G.IsBipartite) (hconn : IsKConnected G 3)
    (hplanar : IsPlanar G) : G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end BarnettesConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct; the notes' remarks (3-connectivity forcing ≥ 4 vertices, harmlessness of IsHamiltonian's singleton convention, need for a bespoke planarity definition) all check out against the Lean definitions.
modeling_decisions: Planarity is defined topologically, exactly as the background article defines it ("can be embedded into the Euclidean plane without any crossings"): a `PlaneEmbedding G` consists of an injective vertex map V → ℝ², and for every edge e ∈ G.edgeSet an injective continuous arc I → ℝ² whose two ends are the images of the ends of e (stated symmetrically via `Sym2.map`), such that interior points of arcs are never vertex images and any point shared by two distinct arcs is a vertex image (hence a common end). `IsPlanar G := Nonempty (PlaneEmbedding G)`. This was chosen over a Kuratowski/Wagner-style definition (which would rest on a deep theorem and would also need bespoke subdivision/minor machinery absent from Mathlib) and over combinatorial embeddings (rotation systems).

3-connectivity uses the repository's `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3` from FormalConjecturesForMathlib: 3 < |V| and deletion of any set of < 3 vertices leaves a connected graph. This matches the standard notion of 3-vertex-connected (polyhedral, per the article) and rules out degenerate graphs such as K₄-sized or smaller cases with ≤ 3 vertices; K₄ itself is excluded only by bipartiteness, as intended.
Cubic is `G.IsRegularOfDegree 3`; bipartite is Mathlib's `G.IsBipartite` (2-colorable). Both need no finiteness beyond `Fintype V` and `DecidableRel G.Adj`.

Conclusion is Mathlib's `G.IsHamiltonian` (`Fintype.card V ≠ 1 → ∃ a p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle`). Since IsKConnected forces |V| > 3, the singleton convention is vacuous and the conclusion is exactly the existence of a Hamiltonian cycle.

The bespoke planarity definitions are generic and would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/; they are kept in the problem file only because the task restricts writes to the single candidate file. Two small sanity statements (`isPlanar_bot` as a test, `IsPlanar.mono` as API) are included and fully proved, per the repository's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.
The Kelmans and dual tree-partition equivalent forms and the Barnette–Goodey conjecture mentioned in the article are not formalized, in line with the decomposition table.

# Barnette's conjecture

-/

namespace BarnettesConjecture

open Set

/-- A finite simple graph is planar if it has a crossing-free drawing in the real plane.
Vertices are represented by distinct points and edges by simple continuous arcs. The interior of
an edge contains no vertex, and the interiors of distinct edges do not intersect. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (vertex : V → ℝ × ℝ)
    (edge : G.edgeSet → Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ × ℝ),
    Function.Injective vertex ∧
    (∀ e, Continuous (edge e)) ∧
    (∀ e, Function.Injective (edge e)) ∧
    (∀ e v,
      v ∈ e.1 ↔
        vertex v = edge e ⟨0, by norm_num⟩ ∨ vertex v = edge e ⟨1, by norm_num⟩) ∧
    (∀ e t v, edge e t = vertex v →
      t = ⟨0, by norm_num⟩ ∨ t = ⟨1, by norm_num⟩) ∧
    (∀ e f, e ≠ f → ∀ s t, edge e s = edge f t →
      (s = ⟨0, by norm_num⟩ ∨ s = ⟨1, by norm_num⟩) ∧
      (t = ⟨0, by norm_num⟩ ∨ t = ⟨1, by norm_num⟩))

/--
**Barnette's conjecture.** Every finite cubic bipartite three-vertex-connected planar simple graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem barnettes_conjecture :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G.IsRegularOfDegree 3 → G.IsBipartite → G.IsKConnected 3 → IsPlanar G → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end BarnettesConjecture
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the terse list entry using the background article: “three-connected” means 3-vertex-connected, formalized by the repository helper `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3`. This requires more than three vertices and connectedness after deleting any set of fewer than three vertices.

Interpreted “planar” by the standard crossing-free topological drawing definition in the real plane: vertices map injectively to points and each edge is a continuous injective arc on `[0,1]`, with vertices only at edge endpoints and distinct edge interiors disjoint.
Used finite simple graphs (`Fintype V` and `SimpleGraph V`), Mathlib’s `SimpleGraph.IsRegularOfDegree 3`, `SimpleGraph.IsBipartite`, and `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian`.
Included `DecidableEq V` and `DecidableRel G.Adj` only to supply Mathlib’s finite-degree and Hamiltonicity APIs; these impose no mathematical restriction on finite graphs.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Barnette's conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Barnette's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnette%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

open SimpleGraph

namespace BarnettesConjecture

/--
A finite simple graph is planar if it has a crossing-free drawing in the real plane. Vertices
are represented by distinct points. Each edge is represented by an embedded interval arc whose
endpoints are exactly the points representing its incident vertices. An arc contains no other
vertex points, and two distinct arcs intersect exactly at the points representing their common
endpoints.
-/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ pos : V → ℝ × ℝ, Function.Injective pos ∧
    ∃ arc : G.edgeSet → (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ × ℝ),
      (∀ e, Topology.IsEmbedding (arc e)) ∧
      (∀ e, arc e '' {t | (t : ℝ) = 0 ∨ (t : ℝ) = 1} =
        pos '' {v | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}) ∧
      (∀ e v, pos v ∈ Set.range (arc e) ↔ v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) ∧
      ∀ e f, e ≠ f → Set.range (arc e) ∩ Set.range (arc f) =
        pos '' {v | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V) ∧ v ∈ (f : Sym2 V)}

/--
**Barnette's conjecture.** Every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph has a Hamiltonian
cycle.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem barnettes_conjecture :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G.IsRegularOfDegree 3 → G.IsBipartite → G.IsKConnected 3 → IsPlanar G → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

distinct arcs meet only at common endpoints. -/

  /-- The point of the plane at which a vertex is drawn. -/
  pos : V → ℝ²
  pos_injective : Function.Injective pos
  /-- The arc of the plane along which an edge is drawn. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²
  exists_path_range_eq_arc : ∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (u v : V), (e : Sym2 V) = s(u, v) →
    ∃ γ : Path (pos u) (pos v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc e
  mem_of_pos_mem_arc : ∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V), pos w ∈ arc e → w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  eq_pos_of_mem_arc_inter : ∀ (e f : G.edgeSet), e ≠ f → ∀ x ∈ arc e ∩ arc f,
    ∃ w : V, w ∈ (e : Sym2 V) ∧ w ∈ (f : Sym2 V) ∧ pos w = x

def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=

theorem IsPlanar.anti {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsPlanar H := by
  obtain ⟨E⟩ := hG

  have hlift : Function.Injective lift := fun e f hef => Subtype.ext (by simpa [lift] using hef)

    pos := E.pos
    pos_injective := E.pos_injective
    arc := fun e => E.arc (lift e)
    exists_path_range_eq_arc := fun e u v huv => E.exists_path_range_eq_arc (lift e) u v huv
    mem_of_pos_mem_arc := fun e w hw => E.mem_of_pos_mem_arc (lift e) w hw
    eq_pos_of_mem_arc_inter := fun e f hef x hx =>
      E.eq_pos_of_mem_arc_inter (lift e) (lift f) (hlift.ne hef) x hx }⟩

theorem isPlanar_bot (n : ℕ) : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) := by
  have hne : (EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 2) (1 : ℝ)) ≠ 0 := by

    have := congrFun (congrArg (⇑) h) 0
    simp at this

    mem_of_pos_mem_arc := fun e => absurd e.2 (by simp)

variable {V : Type*}

/--

The vertices are sent to distinct points of the plane. Each edge is drawn as an arc, that is, a
continuous injective image of the unit interval `[0, 1]`, whose two ends are the images of the two
endpoints of the edge. No arc passes through the image of a vertex other than its own endpoints,
and two different arcs meet only at the images of vertices, which are then endpoints of both edges.
-/
structure PlanarEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The position of each vertex in the plane. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  /-- The arc drawing each edge. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  continuous_arc (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The ends of the arc of an edge are the images of the endpoints of that edge. -/
  arc_zero_one (e : G.edgeSet) :
    ∃ u v, (e : Sym2 V) = s(u, v) ∧ arc e 0 = vertex u ∧ arc e 1 = vertex v
  /-- An arc meets the image of a vertex only if that vertex is an endpoint of its edge. -/
  mem_of_vertex_mem_range (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V) : vertex w ∈ Set.range (arc e) → w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  /-- Two different arcs meet only at images of vertices. -/
  mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter (e e' : G.edgeSet) (he : e ≠ e') (p : ℝ²)
    (hp : p ∈ Set.range (arc e) ∩ Set.range (arc e')) : p ∈ Set.range vertex

def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Barnette's conjecture

Barnette's conjecture concerns Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite polyhedral graphs.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Barnette's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnette%27s_conjecture)
-/

namespace BarnettesConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
A spherical rotation system for a finite simple graph. The equivalence `rotation` cyclically
orders the outgoing darts at each vertex. The face permutation first reverses a dart and then
applies the local rotation; `faces` contains exactly one representative of each of its orbits.
The final equality is Euler's formula.

For a connected finite graph with at least one edge, existence of such a rotation system is
equivalent to planarity.
-/
def HasSphericalRotationSystem {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  ∃ (rotation : G.Dart ≃ G.Dart) (faces : Finset G.Dart),
    (∀ d, (rotation d).fst = d.fst) ∧
    (∀ d e, d.fst = e.fst → ∃ n : ℕ, rotation^[n] d = e) ∧
    (∀ d, ∃! f, f ∈ faces ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, (fun x => rotation x.symm)^[n] d = f) ∧
    (Fintype.card V : ℤ) - (G.edgeFinset.card : ℤ) + (faces.card : ℤ) = 2

/--
**Barnette's conjecture.** Every finite simple graph that is cubic (3-regular), bipartite,
3-vertex-connected, and planar has a Hamiltonian cycle. Planarity is expressed by a spherical
rotation system.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem barnettes_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbipartite : G.IsBipartite)
    (hconnected : G.IsKConnected 3) (hplanar : HasSphericalRotationSystem G) :
    G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end BarnettesConjecture
modeling_decisions: Graphs are modeled as finite simple graphs, as prescribed by the decomposition and consistent with the standard finite meaning of Barnette's conjecture.

Cubic means `SimpleGraph.IsRegularOfDegree 3`; bipartite means `SimpleGraph.IsBipartite`; three-connected means the repository helper `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3`, i.e. more than three vertices and connected after deleting fewer than three vertices.

Because neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has graph planarity or simple-graph minors, planarity is represented by a spherical rotation system: a cyclic order of outgoing darts at every vertex whose reverse-then-rotate face permutation satisfies Euler's formula. On the connected, nonempty graphs forced by the other hypotheses, this is equivalent to ordinary planar embeddability.
The conclusion uses Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian`. Its special singleton convention is irrelevant because `IsKConnected G 3` forces more than three vertices.
The article's equivalent face-parity, polyhedral, Kelmans, and dual-tree-partition formulations are not included because the source slot asks only for the direct graph statement.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Dart` supplies oriented edges, but there is no combinatorial embedding, planar graph, Kuratowski subdivision, or simple-graph minor predicate. Matroid `IsMinor` is not a graph-minor API. A direct geometric edge-drawing definition was also considered but would require substantially more bespoke topology and crossing conditions.

new_definitions.why_needed: A faithful planarity hypothesis is required, but no graph-planarity predicate exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
